scores.accuracy_concern: Hooper 2015 Cochrane found measured fluid intake was not useful as a single test for dehydration, so cup counting must be framed as making sure enough is drunk, not as a way to detect dehydration; ESPEN 1.6 L and 2.0 L figures need the full text; any cup count needs a sourced cup volume or an illustrative label.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C13-20 as its public-facing version, framing the tally as a way to make sure enough is drunk rather than a dehydration test, with a sourced cup volume.

scores.accuracy_concern: Porter 2017 was in subacute (rehabilitation) wards in Melbourne and Hickson 2011 was a single-site before-and-after study, so do not generalise to all acute wards; the claim that hands-on mealtime help raises intake needs its own hospital source (Simmons 2001 is US nursing homes; Young 2013 unchecked).
scores.sharpen: Name the settings in the post and give one sourced figure for what mealtime assistance achieved, so the alternative is as well evidenced as the critique.

scores.accuracy_concern: GLIM low-BMI thresholds apply to Western populations and a GLIM diagnosis also needs an aetiological criterion; MUST scoring and mid-upper arm circumference guidance need an openable BAPEN copy; the Nicholson line is extraneous here.
scores.sharpen: Lead with a labelled illustrative example of someone who lost 8 kg with a BMI still in the normal range, and say GLIM also needs a cause criterion.

scores.accuracy_concern: The central mechanism (menu nutrient analysis assumes the full portion is eaten) has no source; UK hospital food standards were not openable and differ between the four nations, so 'ask for the options meant for small appetites' may not match what a given hospital offers.
scores.sharpen: Proceed only if an openable UK food standard confirms energy-dense provision for nutritionally vulnerable patients; otherwise fold the request into C13-09 or C13-29.

scores.accuracy_concern: No source yet that family presence or help at hospital mealtimes improves intake; using Langmore 1998 (feeding dependency predicts aspiration pneumonia) to justify an eating handover is a stretch; This is me and John's Campaign wording unverified.
scores.sharpen: Anchor the checklist to This is me or a similar opened source and drop the unsupported claim that family presence raises intake.

scores.accuracy_concern: The silent aspiration caveat has no source found yet; the sign list needs RCSLT or stroke guidance; Simmons 2001 minutes come from US nursing homes, not hospital wards.
scores.sharpen: Tie the observation list to a sourced set of swallowing warning signs and give the silent aspiration caveat a citable source or drop it.

scores.accuracy_concern: Recovery data (87% back to usual diet by 6 months) are from first stroke (Mann 1999) and do not support 'many swallowing problems improve' after other acute illness; verify Robbins 2008 dehydration figures and that its population (dementia or Parkinson's) is stated.
scores.sharpen: Limit the recovery statistic explicitly to stroke and keep the post on the review-date principle, citing RCSLT or IDDSI guidance on review if an openable copy exists.

scores.accuracy_concern: Confirm that 39% in Skelly 2017 refers to scheduled doses, not patients; alternative-route guidance rests on NICE NG71 and Brennan 2010, neither yet opened; no conversion doses should appear; overlaps with C06 medicines.
scores.sharpen: Verify the 39% denominator and add one sourced consequence of missed doses (such as worsening rigidity or swallow) so the length-of-stay finding does not undercut the urgency.

scores.accuracy_concern: Participants were well community-dwelling volunteers in Australia, not inpatients; 39% refers to cheese portions in Bell 2016 and the posture study had 34 participants; UK packaging may differ.
scores.sharpen: Open on the tray with the 4 in 10 figure, make the seated-posture finding the second action, and label the population as well older volunteers in Australia.

scores.accuracy_concern: PROT-AGE and ESPEN figures are expert recommendations above the UK reference intake; trial evidence that extra protein improves function in older people is mixed; 'most need fewer calories' needs the SACN source.
scores.sharpen: Add a concrete, sourced example of protein in familiar foods and state that trial evidence for extra protein improving strength is mixed.

scores.accuracy_concern: Evidence is mainly from people with cancer (McCann 1994, 32 patients; Bruera 2013 hospice RCT); NICE NG31 needs a published copy; the post must not imply assisted hydration is never appropriate.
scores.sharpen: Coordinate with C19 so this runs once, and add one line that fluids by drip are a separate decision families can discuss with the team.

scores.accuracy_concern: Ekberg 2002 surveyed people of mixed ages in clinics and nursing homes over 20 years ago, so do not present it as a study of older people only; Wright 2005 had 55 patients.
scores.sharpen: Turn the three findings into three specific questions for a swallowing review, and state the survey date and mixed ages.

scores.accuracy_concern: Confirm whether 57.3% and 30.8% in Serrano Santos 2016 are per-administration error rates (small study, 166 residents); crushing and thickener interaction claims still need a pharmacy or laboratory source.
scores.sharpen: Confirm the denominators and add one sourced example of a tablet that must not be crushed.

scores.accuracy_concern: Cao 2022 also found low-certainty evidence of fewer pneumonia deaths at 24 months, and Zimmerman 2020 had a post hoc first-year reduction; both need stating so the post reads as uncertain, not as evidence of no effect.
scores.sharpen: Include the low-certainty finding on pneumonia deaths and the post hoc first-year signal, so the claim is 'uncertain' rather than 'does not work'.

scores.accuracy_concern: Maeda 2016 is a retrospective cohort whose title uses causal language ('leads to'); confounding by illness severity remains despite weighting; the title 'a treatment with side effects' overclaims; Koyama 2015 not found yet.
scores.sharpen: Retitle to avoid the causal 'side effects' framing, state confounding by severity in the post, and consider sharing the complete-order card with C13-08.

scores.accuracy_concern: Langmore 1998 is observational in mostly male US veterans; dependence for oral care is a marker of risk, and the position that mouth care prevents aspiration pneumonia conflicts with the uncertain trial evidence in C13-14; odds ratios must not become 'times more likely'.
scores.sharpen: Present feeding and mouth-care dependency as markers of risk from an observational study, and avoid claiming mouth care prevents pneumonia, given C13-14.

scores.accuracy_concern: Throat colonisation is not pneumonia; Leibovitz 2003 is a small Israeli study; nasogastric feeding in UK care homes is uncommon, so PEG is the more relevant case; avoid implying mouth care prevents pneumonia given C13-14.
scores.sharpen: Justify daily mouth care by comfort and hygiene first, say colonisation is not infection, and centre the example on PEG feeding.

scores.values_concern: Sensitive decision: wording must keep careful hand feeding as active care so declining a tube never reads as withdrawing care (the draft already does this).
scores.accuracy_concern: Check the certainty grading Davies 2021 gives for the pressure ulcer and pneumonia findings; all evidence is non-randomised; NICE NG97 wording needs confirming.
scores.sharpen: Add the confirmed NICE NG97 wording and one line on what careful hand feeding looks like when the person eats very little.

scores.accuracy_concern: RCSLT 2021 and RCP 2021 documents not yet opened; capacity law differs between Scotland and England and Wales, so name both or neither.
scores.sharpen: Obtain openable copies of the RCSLT and RCP guidance and add a labelled illustrative example to make the sequence concrete.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'Missing drinks between meals' came from one small study (71 people); measured serum osmolality is not always available, so a validated calculated osmolarity equation needs its own source.
scores.sharpen: Add the validated calculated osmolarity equation with its source so practitioners have a usable test when measured osmolality is unavailable.

scores.accuracy_concern: NICE CG32 wording and high-risk criteria need an opened copy; some later guidance (ASPEN 2020) argues the NICE criteria overidentify risk, which could be acknowledged.
scores.sharpen: Add a recognisable geriatric admission scenario and check the CG32 wording against an opened copy.

scores.accuracy_concern: Verify the exact age and sex groups in which Nicholson 2018 found a positive predictive value above 3%; the NG12 threshold needs an opened source; overlaps with C13-03 on measured weight.
scores.sharpen: Verify the age and sex bands for the 3% figure and keep the proportional-investigation point explicit.

scores.accuracy_concern: Doty 1984 measured smell identification, not flavour perception at meals; trials of flavour enhancement on intake are mixed, so tips must be framed as things to try; 'often a loss of smell' is an attribution to soften.
scores.sharpen: Frame flavour tips as things to try, say the evidence on intake is mixed, and coordinate with C14 on the senses.

scores.accuracy_concern: Tan 2018 reports associations; saliva protection and sugary-sweet decay claims need Delivering better oral health or another dental source.
scores.sharpen: Name one or two common drug types in plain words and source the decay advice to Delivering better oral health.

scores.accuracy_concern: Adult Dental Health Survey figures are not yet verified (commonly quoted as 37% of adults with no natural teeth in 1968 and 6% in 2009, all adults, not older people only); the root decay claim needs a source.
scores.sharpen: Verify the survey figures from an opened report and lead with the chart of falling tooth loss, keeping the brushing checklist.

scores.values_concern: Keep the 'less helpful' comic panel from portraying the care worker as careless; show the approach, not a blameworthy person.
scores.accuracy_concern: 'Twice the odds' must not become 'twice as likely'; the named techniques need the intervention description paper, not only the trial abstract.
scores.sharpen: Open on the recognisable moment of the toothbrush being pushed away and name two techniques in the caption, sourced to the intervention paper.

scores.accuracy_concern: Iinuma 2015 is observational despite its title ('doubles the risk'); overnight wearers may differ in health or care; the claim that dentures are lost in hospital needs a source or should be dropped.
scores.sharpen: Avoid the paper's 'doubles' wording and add that other differences between overnight wearers and others may explain part of the link.

scores.accuracy_concern: Hip bone density fell by about 2.6% with aerobic exercise alone in Villareal 2017, not 3%; all three exercise groups also dieted; participants were volunteers able to exercise.
scores.sharpen: Correct the hip bone figure and state that all groups dieted, so the comparison is between types of exercise.

scores.accuracy_concern: Hubbard 2012 was industry-linked and pooled research settings where supplement intake may exceed routine care; the energy-density link comes from unmatched studies; delivery tips lack a source.
scores.sharpen: Say that 67% comes from research settings and cite any delivery tip, such as small volumes at medicine rounds, or drop it.

scores.accuracy_concern: EFFORT was open-label, mortality was a secondary outcome, and participants were general medical inpatients (age profile to confirm, median about 75) in Switzerland.
scores.sharpen: Confirm the age profile and say plainly that the trial was open-label and that deaths were a secondary outcome.

scores.values_concern: Criticism should target dental access and systems, not care home staff.
scores.accuracy_concern: The CQC 'Smiling matters' figures are unverified and the report was not openable; without them the post rests on NICE NG48 alone, which does not show a gap.
scores.sharpen: Hold until the CQC figures are verified from an opened copy; otherwise fold the three questions into C13-25.

scores.accuracy_concern: Nijs 2006 enrolled residents without dementia in five Dutch homes; the 6.1-unit quality of life gain needs a plain meaning; single trial from 2006.
scores.sharpen: Explain the quality of life gain in plain words and state early that residents did not have dementia.

scores.values_concern: Keep the tone generous to families and staff who use contrasting plates.
scores.accuracy_concern: 'Not established' needs a systematic review of mealtime interventions in dementia (Abdelhamid 2016 unchecked); do not slide from 'little evidence' to 'does not work'.
scores.sharpen: Add one line from a systematic review of mealtime interventions in dementia so 'not established' is sourced.

scores.accuracy_concern: Gillman 2017 found low-quality evidence in mostly rehabilitation inpatients; its title ('does not result in aspiration pneumonia') overclaims and should not be echoed.
scores.sharpen: Take the selection criteria from the Gillman review for the diagram and phrase the result as 'did not show an increase'.

scores.accuracy_concern: ESPEN, ADA and Diabetes UK wording still to confirm; the hypoglycaemia point needs a source specific to insulin and sulfonylureas.
scores.sharpen: Confirm the guideline wording and add a sourced line on low blood sugar risk with insulin or sulfonylureas when intake falls.

scores.accuracy_concern: Simmons 2001 is a small 2001 US study in which research staff gave the one-to-one help over two days; 'half ate more' should keep 'significantly' and not be generalised to UK wards or care homes.
scores.sharpen: Say that the 38 minutes came from research staff in a 2001 US study, and add a more recent or UK figure if one can be sourced.

allocation_reason: 33 of 36 candidates reach 36 or more with no disqualifying flag and 17 score 44.5 or more, so the category easily fills the 14-post maximum even after setting aside the cross-category ideas (C13-08 medicines, C13-11 end of life, C13-23 senses, C13-28 weight loss). Note: with the stated weights the formula's true maximum is 55, not 50.
balance_note: The top 14 by score (33, 14, 09, 36, 02, 11, 18, 20, 08, 32, 12, 23, 30, 26) is 6 practitioner, 6 both and only 2 public (C13-23, C13-26). Four of the top eight are evidence corrections (33, 14, 02, 20), so the set leans sceptical. To get closer to the collection's balance, swap C13-30 (a general inpatient trial) for C13-27 (dentures at night, public), and if C06 or C19 take C13-08 or C13-11, replace them with C13-17 or C13-01 (rewritten as the public twin of C13-20). No Ask this or Who gets left out post makes the top 14; C13-07 and C13-24 are the best public Ask this options if the series needs one here. Coherence: if C13-14 runs, word any selected mouth care or denture posts (16, 17, 27) as associations and do not justify mouth care by pneumonia prevention.
